hint.label: Coral reef system
text: A coral reef system is a living underwater structure formed by tiny animals called coral polyps. They build hard structures that provide a home for thousands of marine species.

atoms.b: The Great Barrier Reef is the world’s ((++largest smallest)) coral reef system and stretches over 2,300 km. It is longer than the entire UK and even visible from space.
This reef alone contains 900 islands and around 9,000 types of marine life. It is home to roughly 10% of the world’s ((++fish bird)) species.
The epaulette shark is unique to the Great Barrier Reef and is famous for being able to walk on land using its fins. It can also ((++survive die)) without oxygen for up to two hours.

atoms.a: Uluru is a huge sandstone rock that stands almost 350 metres tall. It is estimated to be more than 500 million years old.
atoms.sound: Uluru is a huge sand stone rock that stands almost 350 metres tall. It is estimated to be more than 500 million years old.

atoms.a: It lies in the Outback, a vast and dry interior region covering around two thirds of Australia.
Uluru is sacred to the Aboriginal peoples in the area, so it is forbidden to climb it out of respect.

hint.label: Aboriginal peoples
hint.text: Aboriginal peoples are Indigenous Australians whose ancestors have lived on the continent for at least 65,000 years.

atoms.a: The desert around Uluru is home to the thorny devil. This small, spiky lizard has adapted to absorb water through its skin.

hint.label: Marsupial
hint.text: A marsupial is a type of mammal whose young are born underdeveloped and usually continue growing in the mother’s belly pouch.

atoms.b: Koalas are marsupials that typically live in eastern Australia’s eucalyptus forests. They mainly eat the leaves from these trees and can ((++sleep run)) up to 20 hours a day.
The red kangaroo is another famous Australian marsupial and the ((++largest smallest)) on Earth. It can leap up to nine metres forwards but struggles to move backwards.
Australia has been isolated from other continents for millions of years. This is why over 80% of its mammals, reptiles, amphibians and plants exist ((++nowhere everywhere)) else.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: Much of Australia’s population live in big cities in the south-east, where the climate is milder and there are more jobs. Around 40% of Australians live in Sydney and Melbourne alone, the country’s two largest cities.

Sydney is Australia’s most-populated city, with over 5.5 million residents. It is home to several iconic landmarks, including the Sydney Opera House and Sydney Harbour Bridge. Sydney also has the famous Bondi Beach, which is known for its golden sand and surfing culture.

Melbourne, Australia’s second-largest city, is often described as the nation’s cultural capital because of its famous street art, museums and live entertainment. It is also the home of “Aussie Rules” Football, Australia’s most-watched sport.

Despite having a population of fewer than 500,000 people, Canberra is the capital of Australia. It was specifically planned and built for this purpose as a compromise between the rival cities of Sydney and Melbourne. Canberra is home to Parliament House, where politicians meet to discuss new laws.
